topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetics, environmental exposures, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer causation by exploring the interplay between intrinsic mutational processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, illustrated in detail through the etiology and mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and promotional carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical and cellular mechanisms by which mutagens, metabolic activation pathways, and tumour promoters induce DNA damage and support malignancy.

topics.label: Methods for detecting, testing, and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens, test mutagenicity, and evaluate associated health risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary of the lecture's central themes concerning environmental cancer risks and carcinogen potency.
